title: Don't itemize? Charity gifts can count in 2026
label: Year-end tax move

beats.note: Cash gifts to qualified charities. Donor-advised funds don't count.

items.t: Give by check, card or bank transfer
Keep the bank record or charity letter
$250 or more? Get a written receipt
items.s: From the charity, before you file.

cta.sub: We'll DM you our year-end planning page.

captions.instagram:
Take the standard deduction? Starting with 2026, your charity gifts can still count.

✔️ Non-itemizers can deduct up to $1,000 of cash gifts to qualified charities ($2,000 married filing jointly).
✔️ Gifts to donor-advised funds don't count for this one, and it's for cash gifts, not donated goods.
✔️ Give by check, card or bank transfer and keep the bank record or the charity's letter.
✔️ $250 or more in one gift? Get a written acknowledgment from the charity.

More moves to make by Dec. 31 on our year-end planning page.

sources.fact: Beginning with tax year 2026, if you don't itemize you may deduct up to $1,000 ($2,000 joint) of cash contributions to qualified organizations; monetary gifts need a bank record or written communication; $250 or more needs a contemporaneous written acknowledgment (updated 24-Sep-2026); read 2026-10-30

OBBB provisions: bronze and catastrophic plans HSA-compatible from Jan. 1, 2026; non-itemizers may deduct up to $1,000 ($2,000 MFJ) of cash gifts to charity from tax year 2026, donor-advised funds and supporting organizations excluded; read 2026-10-30
